simple.meaning: לַפִּיד (lappîyd) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a flambeau , lamp or flame.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 15:17. The surrounding context includes family line, kingship, mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לַפִּיד (H3940) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: לַפִּיד (lappîyd) / H3940 is traced through Genesis 15:17, Exodus 20:18, Judges 7:16, Judges 7:20 with generated occurrence evidence.

timeline.evidenceText: It came to pass that, when the sun went down, and it was dark, behold, a smoking furnace and a flaming torch passed between these pieces.
All the people perceived the thunderings, the lightnings, the sound of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking. When the people saw it, they trembled, and stayed at a distance.
He divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put into the hands of all them trumpets and empty pitchers, with torches within the pitchers.

The three companies blew the trumpets, broke the pitchers, and held the torches in their left hands and the trumpets in their right hands with which to blow; and they shouted, “The sword of Yahweh and of Gideon!”
Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, and took torches, and turned tail to tail, and put a torch in the middle between every two tails.
Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, and took torches, and turned tail to tail, and put a torch in the middle between every two tails.
When he had set the torches on fire, he let them go into the standing grain of the Philistines, and burned up both the shocks and the standing grain, and also the olive groves.
In the thought of him who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune.
Who has first given to me, that I should repay him?
For Zion’s sake I will not hold my peace,

As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, like the appearance of torches. The fire went up and down among the living creatures. The fire was bright, and lightning went out of the fire.

His body also was like the beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as flaming torches. His arms and his feet were like burnished bronze. The voice of his words was like the voice of a multitude.
He summons his picked troops. They stumble on their way. They dash to its wall, and the protective shield is put in place.

In that day I will make the chieftains of Judah like a pan of fire among wood, and like a flaming torch among sheaves; and they will devour all the surrounding peoples, on the right hand and on the left; and Jerusalem will yet again dwell in their own place, even in Jerusalem.

definitions.full: H3940. lappid לַמּיד noun masculine Judg 15:4 torch (Late Hebrew id. ); — ׳ל absolute 15:4 ; Isa 62:1 ; construct Gen 15:17 ; Zech 12:6 ; plural לַמִּידִים Judg 15:5 2 t., לַמִּידִם Exod 20:18 , לַמִּדִים Judg 7:16 3 t.; construct לַמִּידֵי Dan 10:6 : — torch , Judg 7:16 , 20 ; 15:4 (twice in verse); 15:5 (kindled, בְּ אֵשׁ ׳הִבְעִיר ); אֵשׁ לַמִּיד Gen 15:17 ( + תַּנּוּר עָשָׁן, ; J E), Zech 12:6 (simile of conquering power of [chiefs of] Judah; || אֵשׁ כִּיּוֺר ), אֵשׁ לַמִּידֵי Dan 10:6 (simile of eyes of angel in vision; || בָרָק כְּמַרְאֵה וּפָנָיו ); simile of flashes (reflected from) darting chariots Nahum 2:15 (|| בְּרָקִים ); ׳ל of lightning-flashes Exod 20:18 (E; + קוֺלֹת thunder-peals ); of flashing water-drops expelled by snortings of crocodile Job 41:11 (|| אֵשׁ כִּידוֺדֵי ); of flame between cherubim Ezek 1:13 (|| אֵשׁ אֵשׁ, גַּחֲלֵיֿ ); simile of Zion's glorious deliverance Isa 62:1 (|| נֹגַהּ ). — לַמִּיד Job 12:5 see below מִּיד .
definitions.rootNote: or לַפִּד ; from an unused root probably meaning to shine ;
